newsitem.title: USA: Shoney's holder group seeks special meeting.
newsitem.headline: Shoney's holder group seeks special meeting.

text.p: The son and the wife of the founder of restaurant chain Shoney's Inc said Monday they plan to seek a special shareholders' meeting to ask for the removal of company's directors.
In a statement, Raymond and Betty Schoenbaum said they are making preliminary filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission so they can solicit support from other shareholders.
They said they hold a combined eight percent stake in Shoney's, but Tennesee's corporation law requires at least 10 percent of shareholders to call a special meeting.
Shoney's, which owns and operates about 1,400 restaurants, is based in Nashville, Tenn. In March, the company reported a first quarter net loss of $13.8 million on $363.3 million of revenues.
The Schoenbaums, who have formed a shareholders' committee, said that, if the meeting is called, they would seek to replace Shoney's seven-member board with their own nominees.
They said they "have been disappointed with Shoney's operating performance and stock price in recent years."
"As the son and wife of Alex Schoenbaum, Shoney's founder, we regard Shoney's as a legacy of our family and its struggles in recent years have been personally very distressing to us," they said.
